author: conductor
title: H14 is scope discipline, not a sandbox — stated honestly rather than tightened
statement:
H14's purpose is SCOPE DISCIPLINE: keep agents on the project's declared toolchain commands, deny shell chaining and redirection, deny find/sed/awk. It is NOT code-execution containment, it never was, and it is not being made into one. The hook's header now says so explicitly so no future design leans on it as a sandbox.

WHY NOT TIGHTEN (the load-bearing reason): a declared run command is an interpreter invocation, and every Bash-holding agent also holds Write. `node --test <file>` executes that file's top-level code even with no tests in it (research_finding 08893fc0, probed on Node 24), and the shipped node adapter declares `test: 'node --test'`, so arbitrary execution is reachable in every Sterling node project by default. Path-scoping the argument cannot fix this: the debugger's LEGITIMATE probe road is precisely 'write a file into the session scratchpad, run it through the declared command'. Any rule permissive enough to allow the debugger to work is permissive enough to allow arbitrary execution. The two are the same capability.

So the choice was never 'leaky vs sealed', it was 'honest vs misleading'. A gate that cannot change the outcome it appears to guard is ceremony (P1), and a gate that misrepresents what it enforces is worse than none — it invites future designs to rely on protection that is not there.

WHAT ACTUALLY CONTAINS AGENTS: H3 (write contract — denies out-of-repo writes in RUN mode, allows them in DIRECT mode at h3:63), H5 (frozen tests), H17 (bash write sweep), the per-agent tool grants, and the fact that Sterling dispatches agents already trusted to author code.

COMSOFT RESIDUE: that project's hand-added `probe: "node"` run command is derivative of this, not causal — it only drops the `--test` requirement. It is left in place deliberately: Comsoft's existing debug harnesses are invoked as `node scripts/debug-*.mjs`, and removing the entry would break them for no security gain, since `node --test` already provides the same capability.

alternatives_rejected.option: Scope the allowlist to interpreter + argument path (e.g. permit `node --test` only under test globs or the session scratchpad)
alternatives_rejected.reason: Ineffective by construction. The scratchpad MUST stay permitted or the debugger cannot instrument, and the agent can write whatever it likes into the scratchpad — so the narrowed rule still permits arbitrary execution while adding matching logic to a BLOCKING hook where a mistake makes enforcement vanish silently. Cost with no outcome change (P1). This was the option the council's open research question was gating; the question turned out to be moot once the write-then-execute path was traced.

alternatives_rejected.option: Remove `node --test` from the shipped node adapter's run_commands
alternatives_rejected.reason: Removes the ability to run tests — the toolchain's entire purpose. Absurd on its face; recorded only to show the allowlist cannot be both useful and containing.

alternatives_rejected.option: Narrow H3's direct-mode out-of-repo write allowance so agents cannot author scratchpad files
alternatives_rejected.reason: Would break the debugger's probe road (its core loop) and the scratchpad convention generally, to close one of several equivalent paths — an agent with repo-write can equally author and execute an in-repo file. Symptom-chasing, and it trades a real capability for no containment.

alternatives_rejected.option: Say nothing and leave the header implying deny-by-default containment
alternatives_rejected.reason: The status quo, and the actual defect. The misleading framing already produced one bad decision this session: the debugger's per-project probe opt-in was designed to work around a restriction that does not exist. An unstated limitation is not an accepted one.

rationale: Surfaced by council wf_0d90ab18-436 (black hat headline: 'H14's deny-by-default is nominal'), then verified directly rather than accepted — the `node --test` execution behaviour by live probe, the H3 direct-vs-run asymmetry by reading h3:51 and h3:63, and the end-to-end reachability by dispatching a real debugger subagent that wrote a scratchpad probe and executed it (EXEC=YES). Board item 8423f412 offered three dispositions; tracing the write-then-execute path eliminated two of them as ineffective, leaving honesty. Conduct rule applied: disclose limitations, do not bury them — here the disclosure lands in the enforcement code itself, where the next designer will read it.
